1.note: The phrase **Thus says Yahweh** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.

Isaiah is not distinguishing this **anointed** from another anointed one that is not **Cyrus**. He is reminding the reader that Yahweh’s anointed one is Cyrus. Be sure that this is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [to his anointed one, Cyrus]

Here Yahweh is speaking of choosing and empowering Cyrus as if he had taken hold of his **right hand**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [whom I have chosen and empowered]

1.q: לְ⁠רַד־לְ⁠פָנָי⁠ו֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם וּ⁠מָתְנֵ֥י מְלָכִ֖ים אֲפַתֵּ֑חַ לִ⁠פְתֹּ֤חַ לְ⁠פָנָי⁠ו֙ דְּלָתַ֔יִם וּ⁠שְׁעָרִ֖ים לֹ֥א יִסָּגֵֽרוּ
1.note: Here, the phrases **to subdue nations to his face** and **to open doors to his face** mark those actions as the purpose for which Yahweh has grasped Cyrus’s right hand. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

Here, **his face** represents Cyrus himself, in the sense of being in his presence or before him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to subdue nations before him]

Here, the **loins of kings** represent the strength that kings have for battle. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and I will take away the strength of kings]

The expression **will not be shut** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and no one will shut the gates]

2.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I will go** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he is personally committed to going before Cyrus. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [I will indeed go before you]

Here Yahweh is speaking of removing the obstacles in Cyrus’s way as if he would **flatten the swollen** ground. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will remove the obstacles before you]

Yahweh is using the adjective **the swollen** as a noun to refer to a certain kind of terrain. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [I will flatten the swollen places]

Some ancient manuscripts read “the swollen.” The ULT follows that reading. Other ancient manuscripts read “the mountains.” If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT. Alternate translation: [the mountains]

Yahweh is using **doors of bronze** and **bars of iron** to represent the strongly fortified cities that they protect. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the defenses of strongly fortified cities, and I will cut through all their barriers]

3.q: וְ⁠נָתַתִּ֤י לְ⁠ךָ֙ אוֹצְר֣וֹת חֹ֔שֶׁךְ וּ⁠מַטְמֻנֵ֖י מִסְתָּרִ֑ים
3.note: The terms **treasures of darkness** and **hoards of secret places** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [And I will give you the treasures stored in dark, secret places]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **darkness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the treasures hidden in dark places]

Here, the phrase **so that you may know** marks what follows as the purpose for which Yahweh will give Cyrus these treasures. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [in order that you may know]

4.note: Here, the phrase **For the sake of** introduces the reason why Yahweh has called Cyrus. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the reason. Alternate translation: [To show favor to my servant Jacob]
The pronoun **you** refers to Cyrus. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [though Cyrus had not known me]

5.note: This could mean: (1) “I will strengthen you for battle” or (2) “I will equip you for battle.”

6.note: Here, the phrase **so that they may know** marks what follows as the purpose for which Yahweh acts on Cyrus’s behalf. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [which will cause them to know]
The pronoun **they** refers to people throughout the world. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [so that people throughout the world may know]

7.q: יוֹצֵ֥ר אוֹר֙ וּ⁠בוֹרֵ֣א חֹ֔שֶׁךְ עֹשֶׂ֥ה שָׁל֖וֹם וּ⁠ב֣וֹרֵא רָ֑ע
7.note: Yahweh is referring to all that he brings about by naming pairs of opposites, **light** and **darkness**, and **peace** and **trouble**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Causing everything that happens, both good things and bad things]

8.q: הַרְעִ֤יפוּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ מִ⁠מַּ֔עַל וּ⁠שְׁחָקִ֖ים יִזְּלוּ צֶ֑דֶק תִּפְתַּח אֶ֣רֶץ וְ⁠יִפְרוּ יֶ֗שַׁע
8.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of the **heavens**, the **skies**, and the **earth** as if they were living things that could obey his commands to **rain down** righteousness and bring forth salvation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will cause righteousness to come down from above and salvation to spring up from the earth]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and let the skies pour down righteous deeds]

Here Yahweh is speaking of salvation and righteousness as if they were crops that the earth could **bear** and make **sprout**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and let salvation come, and let righteousness come about as well]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and let them bear those who are saved]

9.note: Yahweh is using the word **Woe** to express a strong feeling of distress about the judgment that is coming. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [How terrible for]

Here Yahweh is speaking of a human being who argues with God as if that person were merely **a shard among the shards of the ground**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [someone utterly insignificant]

9.q: הֲ⁠יֹאמַ֨ר חֹ֤מֶר לְ⁠יֹֽצְר⁠וֹ֙ מַֽה תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה וּ⁠פָעָלְ⁠ךָ֖ אֵין יָדַ֥יִם לֽ⁠וֹ
9.note: Yahweh is using the question form to assert that no human being has the right to challenge God, just as clay has no right to challenge the potter who shapes it. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [The clay cannot say to its fashioner, “What are you making?” or “Your work, there are no hands to it.”]

Here Yahweh is speaking of himself as the maker of human beings, and of people as the things he has made, as if he were a potter and they were the **clay** that he shapes. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Shall a person say to his maker]

10.q: ה֛וֹי אֹמֵ֥ר לְ⁠אָ֖ב מַה תּוֹלִ֑יד וּ⁠לְ⁠אִשָּׁ֖ה מַה תְּחִילִֽי⁠ן
10.note: Yahweh is using the question form to declare that no one has the right to question what God is doing, just as a child has no right to question its own parents. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Woe to the one saying to a father, “You should not be begetting!” or to a woman, “You should not be writhing in labor!”]
See how you translated the similar expression in 45:9.

11.note: See how you translated the similar expression in [45:1](ta:45).

11.q: הָ⁠אֹתִיּ֣וֹת שְׁאָל֔וּ⁠נִי עַל בָּנַ֛⁠י וְ⁠עַל פֹּ֥עַל יָדַ֖⁠י תְּצַוֻּֽ⁠נִי
11.note: Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke those who would question or command him about what he does for his people. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You should not ask me the coming things concerning my sons, or command me concerning the work of my hands]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the people he created as if they were his **sons**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the people I created]

Here, **my hands** represents Yahweh himself acting to create. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [what I have made]

12.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I made** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he is the one who made the earth. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [It is I who made the earth]

Here Yahweh is speaking of creating the sky as if the **heavens** were a fabric or tent that he **stretched out**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [It was my own hands that created the heavens]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the stars as if they were an **army** that he commands. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I commanded all the stars in them]

13.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **have awakened** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he is the one who has awakened him. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [I myself have awakened him]

Yahweh is using **awakened him in righteousness** as a common expression of the culture to mean “summoned and empowered him to accomplish what is right.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have roused him to carry out my righteous purpose] or [I have appointed him to do what is right]
The pronoun **him** refers to Cyrus. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [I have awakened Cyrus]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in doing things rightly]

Yahweh is using **and I will straighten all of his ways** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I will remove all obstacles that would prevent him from doing what I have appointed him to do.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will clear every obstacle from his path] or [and I will ensure he succeeds in all I have appointed him to do]

Yahweh is stating the pronoun **he** separately, even though the verb translated as **he will build** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that Cyrus will do Yahweh’s will. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [It is Cyrus who will build]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **captivity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and my captive people]
The phrase **says Yahweh of Armies** indicates that the preceding words are a direct quotation from Yahweh. In your translation, use a natural way of marking direct quotations in your language.

14.note: Yahweh is using **men of stature** as a common expression of the culture to mean men who are tall. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [men who are tall]
The pronoun **you** refers to the people of Zion, that is, Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [will pass over to the people of Israel]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the people of these nations submitting to Israel and becoming its captives as if they would **walk after you** and **pass over in chains**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They will submit to you; they will come to you as captives]

14.q: אַ֣ךְ בָּ֥⁠ךְ אֵ֛ל וְ⁠אֵ֥ין ע֖וֹד אֶ֥פֶס אֱלֹהִֽים
14.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [telling you that God is surely with you and that there is no other, no other God]

15.note: Here Isaiah is speaking of how Yahweh acts in ways that people cannot see as if Yahweh were a **God hiding himself**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [are a God whose actions are hidden from people]

16.note: The pronoun **They** refers to the people who make idols. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The makers of idols will have shame]

The expression **be disgraced** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [suffer disgrace]

Isaiah is using **they will walk in disgrace** as a common expression of the culture to mean that they will be completely put to shame. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they will go about in shame] or [they will be put to shame]

17.note: The expression **will be saved** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will save Israel]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [so that they will be safe forever]

Isaiah is using the possessive form to describe a **salvation of eternities** that is characterized by lasting forever. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [an everlasting salvation]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **eternities** that are characterized by forever. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [forever and ever]

The expression **will not be disgraced** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and no one will disgrace you]

18.note: The phrase **For thus says Yahweh** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.

The repeated pronoun **he** refers to Yahweh, while the pronoun **it** refers to the earth. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh himself established the earth]

Here, the word **For** introduces the reason that supports what Yahweh said in the previous verse. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the reason. Alternate translation: [Because]

19.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of revealing his message in an obscure or hidden way as if he had spoken **in secret, in a place of a land of darkness**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in a secret place that is difficult to find]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **darkness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in a dark land]

19.q: לֹ֥א אָמַ֛רְתִּי לְ⁠זֶ֥רַע יַעֲקֹ֖ב תֹּ֣הוּ בַקְּשׁ֑וּ⁠נִי
19.note: Here there is a quotation within a quotation. If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [I did not tell the seed of Jacob to seek me in emptiness]

20.note: Yahweh is using the adjective **fugitives** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person, those who have survived and escaped. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [those who have escaped from the nations]

21.q: מִ֣י הִשְׁמִיעַ֩ זֹ֨את מִ⁠קֶּ֜דֶם מֵ⁠אָ֣ז הִגִּידָ֗⁠הּ
21.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that he alone foretold these events long ago. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [I made one hear this from antiquity, declared it from then!]

Yahweh is using the question form to affirm that he, Yahweh, is the one who foretold these things. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [It was I, Yahweh]
If it would appear in your language that Yahweh was making a statement and then contradicting it, you could reword this as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [I alone am God]

21.q: וְ⁠אֵֽין־ע֤וֹד אֱלֹהִים֙ מִ⁠בַּלְעָדַ֔⁠י אֵֽל־צַדִּ֣יק וּ⁠מוֹשִׁ֔יעַ אַ֖יִן זוּלָתִֽ⁠י
21.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and you may want to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [And there is no other God except me, a righteous God and a Savior—indeed, there is none besides me]

22.note: The expression **be saved** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Turn to me and I will save you]

Here, the word **for** introduces the reason why the people of the earth should turn to Yahweh. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the reason. Alternate translation: [because]

Yahweh is using **all of the ends of the earth** as a common expression of the culture to mean “people who live everywhere in the world.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [people who live everywhere in the world]

23.note: Here, **my mouth** represents the person who is speaking. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [righteous words have gone out from me]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what is right]

Here Yahweh is speaking of his **word** as if it were a living thing that could **return**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a word that I will not retract]

23.q: לִ⁠י֙ תִּכְרַ֣ע כָּל בֶּ֔רֶךְ תִּשָּׁבַ֖ע כָּל לָשֽׁוֹן
23.note: Here, **every knee** represents every person bowing in submission, and **every tongue** represents every person making a declaration of loyalty. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [every person will bow down to me in submission, and every person will swear allegiance to me]

24.q: אַ֧ךְ בַּ⁠יהוָ֛ה לִ֥⁠י אָמַ֖ר צְדָק֣וֹת וָ⁠עֹ֑ז
24.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **righteousnesses** and **strength**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [One will say of me, ‘Only Yahweh does right and gives strength.’]

Here there is a quotation within a quotation. If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [People will say of me that only in Yahweh are righteousness and strength]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [In me alone,’ Yahweh will say of himself]

24.q: עָדָי⁠ו֙ יָב֣וֹא וְ⁠יֵבֹ֔שׁוּ כֹּ֖ל הַ⁠נֶּחֱרִ֥ים בּֽ⁠וֹ
24.note: Here the author is using the pronouns **one** and **ones** in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [To him people will come, and they will have shame, all of the people who have been hostile toward t him will come to him]

Isaiah is using **the ones having been kindled against him** as a common expression of the culture to mean “those who have been hostile toward him.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [those who have been angry at him] or [those who have opposed him]

The expression **having been kindled** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [those who burned with anger]
The pronoun **him** refers to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [against Yahweh]

25.note: Isaiah is using **In Yahweh** as a common expression of the culture to mean “because of Yahweh” or “by means of Yahweh.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Because of Yahweh] or [By means of Yahweh]

Here Isaiah is speaking of the descendants of Israel as if they were the **seed** that Israel had planted. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all of the descendants of Israel]
